components.description: Eighteen consecutive weeks of maternity leave for a pregnant member, granted by the Dean on request with a medical certificate; restates the Quebec Act respecting labour standards s. 81.4 (unpaid maternity leave of not more than 18 weeks). Governing document: the CUFA collective agreement 2015-2018 (in effect until May 31, 2018; in force on 2018-02-22). Art. 35 governs maternity, paternity and parental leave for faculty. HR-23 (effective 2002-04-22; the 2020 capture still carries that date, so the same version was in force in 2018) applies to all employees unless collective-agreement provisions apply; its maternity, adoption, paternity and extended-parental provisions are recorded for staff (c33-c38, not counted). Only its paid leave for pregnancy medical appointments (cl. 8), on which the agreement is silent, is coded for faculty (c32), following the HR-23 version note.

Path (U8): Art. 35.02 sets three categories (QPIP-eligible, EI-eligible because resident outside Quebec, neither). The coded member is resident in Quebec and eligible for QPIP. EI path, not coded: maternity 100% of nominal salary for the first two weeks (described as the waiting period), then the EI top-up to 95% for up to 15 more weeks, payments from 8 weeks before to 17 weeks after the birth (35.05); parental 100% for the first two weeks if no maternity leave was taken, then the EI top-up to 95% for 35 weeks (35.12). Neither QPIP nor EI: 95% of nominal salary for 10 weeks of maternity leave (35.06).

QPIP: coded at the basic plan (maternity 18 weeks at 70%, paternity 5 at 70%, parental 32: 7 at 70% then 25 at 55%); the special plan (15/3/25 weeks at 75%) is in duration_variants (U2). QPIP has no waiting period (programs.csv), so the benefits start with the leaves. QPIP adoption benefits (37 weeks) are not coded as a separate component; the 37-week adoption supplement is in c13's duration_variants.

Statutory leaves (U4): the agreement relies on the Act respecting labour standards ('no less than those provided for in the relevant government legislation', 35.14 a; HR-23 names the Act). Articles that restate a statutory leave without adding length are coded as the statute (maternity c1 = s. 81.4; paternity c7 = s. 81.2; health extension c14 = s. 81.14.2; special leave c15 = s. 81.5.1). The agreement's two-year parental leave (c10) adds length, so the statutory 52-week parental leave (c11) runs alongside it (S1). The statutory five days at a birth or adoption (c5, two paid) carry the agreement's five fully paid days (c6) within them.

Birth parent chain: maternity leave 18 (QPIP maternity 18 at 70% and the employer supplement to 95% within it) -> supplemental maternity leave 2 at 95% -> parental leave up to 104 (QPIP parental 32 and the supplement to 95% within it; statutory parental leave 52 alongside) -> sick leave up to 4 months if ill at the expected return (35.14 m; pay c21 within it); a reduced-time appointment of up to 30 months may also prolong the parental leave (c18, consecutive_after c10). The special leave for pregnancy risk (c15) and health extension (c14) have no stated length and are unlinked.

Non-birth parent chain: statutory five days at the birth (c5) with the agreement's five fully paid days within it (c6), unlinked to the leaves -> paternity leave up to 5 (QPIP paternity 5 at 70% and the supplement to 95% within it) -> parental leave up to 104 (QPIP parental 32, counted in full, U2, with the supplement within; statutory parental leave 52 alongside).
Art. 35.08 b) refers to the birth parent's 'twenty (20) weeks of maternity leave', consistent with 18 weeks plus the 2-week supplemental leave (c4).

Research appointments (Art. 12.06 d) are excluded from Arts. 32 and 35.08-35.12 unless the external funder agrees; they are not tenure-stream. LTA and visiting appointees are outside the tenure stream. Librarians have parallel tenure and reappointment deferrals (15.02 b-c, 19.05 b); not coded as they are not faculty.

HR-23 provisions summarised, not coded separately: maternity indemnity for staff not eligible for EI (93% to the 10th week, cl. 10); temporary employees' five days at birth or adoption with two paid under the Act respecting labour standards (cl. 28, 31, 38); spouse of an adopting employee four paid working days (cl. 26).
Calendar: the agreement names fall, winter and summer terms but states no term length or quarter/semester kind; calendar omitted.
